a potential bug when I use tikzDevice and knitr (Yihui mentioned I should

Guy

----------

The following code compiles nicely but the "$\\theta$" inside ggplot2's
facets do not propagate properly. I would like to have the greek symbol in
the facets. In other words, I can use "$\\theta$" as arguments to xlab or
ylab, but not for facets.

\documentclass{article}
\begin{document}

<<sasd,dev='tikz'>>=
x=c(0,1)
D=stack(list("$\\theta=0.3$"=dbinom(x,1,0.3),'$\\theta=0.5$'=dbinom(x,1,0.5),'$\\theta=0.9$'=dbinom(x,1,0.9)))
names(D)=c("mass","theta")
D$x=x
qplot(x, mass, data=D, geom='bar', stat='identity', facets=.~theta,
            xlab="$x$",ylab="$p_X(x)$",main='Bernoulli Distribution Mass
Functions')
@

\end{document}

Hi Guy,

I cannot reproduce this bug in the absence of Knitr. Given a slight
modification of your example:

require(ggplot2)
require(tikzDevice)

x=c(0,1)
D=stack(list("$\\theta=0.3$"=dbinom(x,1,0.3),
  '$\\theta=0.5$'=dbinom(x,1,0.5),
  '$\\theta=0.9$'=dbinom(x,1,0.9)))
names(D)=c("mass","theta")
D$x=x

p <- qplot(x, mass, data=D, geom='bar', stat='identity', facets=.~theta,

  xlab="$x$",ylab="$p_X(x)$",
  main='Bernoulli Distribution Mass Functions')

tikz('test.tex', standAlone = TRUE)
print(p)
dev.off()

The standalone file `test.tex` compiles fine and contains the expected
output.

-Charlie

messages.subject: Re: [Tikzdevice-bugs] Tikzdevice not finishing file
messages.body_plain:
On Thu, Apr 12, 2012 at 10:59 AM, Charlie Sharpsteen
<ch...@sharpsteen.net>wrote:

>  Error in createLockFile(lockname) : cannot create lock file****
>>
>> ** **
>>
>> Is this related to the problem above?
>>
>
> It could possibly be the cause. This usually happens when you interrupt R
> while tikz is drawing---this causes filehash to leave a stray lockfile
> which blocks all further text rendering operations.
>
>  There is a fix for this situation in the devel version, but
> unfortunately R-Forge has mysteriously stopped building binary packages for
> us. I have been bugging them about it, but no response so far. Source code
> for the latest devel snapshot is available from GitHub:
>
>   https://github.com/Sharpie/RTikZDevice/zipball/r-forge
>
> -Charlie
>

Just a follow-up note: Binary packages are now available from R-Forge once
again. Development snapshots can be installed using:

    install.packages('tikzDevice', repos = 'http://r-forge.r-project.org')

-Charlie
